Research Vision

My research vision is to make cellular networks predictable, measurable, and controllable to enable reliable next-generation latency-sensitive applications, including AR/VR, cloud services, and connected autonomy. I combine large-scale real-world measurements, cross-layer performance analysis, and programmable 5G/6G experimentation to understand and address challenges in network reliability, latency, and performance. My goal is to develop lightweight, standards-compliant, and practical solutions that leverage AI-driven analytics and closed-loop network control to improve performance, energy efficiency, and reliability in real-world deployments.

Experience

AT&T Labs, Inc.

Research Engineer

2026 - 2026 | Contract

https://about.att.com/sites/labs

*Developed a production-ready anomaly detection pipeline for E911 network KPIs using a lightweight Isolation Forest model, enriched with SIP/CCDR protocol context, including message types, cause codes, and failure indicators. Engineered historical baseline features using z-scores, rolling means, and rolling standard deviations to identify KPI degradation, achieving ~90% anomaly correlation with known network incidents.

*Benchmarked graph-based SSB optimization approaches using Google OR-Tools and SCIP on production network inventory data, incorporating neighbor weights to evaluate optimization performance in terms of execution time, number of configuration changes, and iterations required to reach optimality.
